title: Machine learning nominates synergistic drug combinations in pancreatic cancer cells
summary: Three research groups used machine-learning models trained on 496 measured PANC-1 drug pairs to nominate additional combinations. Of 88 nominated pairs tested, 51 met the study’s synergy threshold. The article also reports 307 synergistic combinations including the 256-pair training screen; the 307 total is not a count of new AI-nominated hits. The result is limited to cell assays.
ai_technology: Random forests; XGBoost; deep neural networks; graph convolutional networks
organization: National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences; University of North Carolina; Massachusetts Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: The primary source reports the study-specific result summarized here.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and broad deployment are not established by this review.
evidence.ai_role: Models trained on measured drug-combination assays rank candidates from a virtual library; nominated combinations are tested in PANC-1 cell assays.

source_review.scope: Full primary publisher article text, abstract, methods, results
